text.title: Freelancer Payment Chase Script Library Worked Examples
text.summary: One complete ladder for a GBP 4,800 net-15 invoice to a UK client that pays after the polite rung, with the three rung texts and a note on every non-obvious value, and one bad ladder showing what the validator and the reviewer reject.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: Invoice 2026-041 for GBP 4,800 under an MSA with net-15 terms (clause 7.2) fell due on 2026-06-15. The client is a UK company, so statutory interest under the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998 applies even though the MSA has no late-fee clause of its own. The sponsor is Dana; accounts payable is a shared mailbox.

example.title: Invoice 2026-041, paid after the polite rung
example.note: All three rungs are drafted and dated up front (due + 3, + 10, + 30) even though only the first was sent: the ladder is planned from the due date, not improvised from the send date (r-three-rungs-clocked-from-due-date).

`late_payment_basis` is a statute, not a clause, because the MSA is silent: the Act grants 8% over base rate plus a GBP 70 fixed sum on a debt of this size, and that exact wording is the only consequence the firm rung and the ledger may quote (r-fees-and-leverage-only-from-contract-or-statute).

The polite rung has one recipient (the person who received the invoice), 84 words, one question, no consequence; the firm rung adds `ap@acme.example` and a pay-by date 6 days after its send date (r-polite-rung-assumes-oversight, r-firm-rung-deadline-and-named-consequence).

`ledger_total_with_interest` 4921.40 is 4800 plus 30 days of statutory interest at the rate in force plus the GBP 70 fixed sum; the final deadline is 14 days and the next step is a county-court claim, sent by email and registered post as the MSA's notice clause requires (r-legal-rung-is-formal-letter-before-action).

Payment landed on 2026-07-05 (20 days after due), so `halted` is true with `halt_reason = paid_in_full` and the firm rung was never sent; the single log entry carries the client's response. `renewal_terms_change = deposit` because this is the client's third invoice averaging over 20 days on net 15 (r-stop-on-payment-dispute-or-exhaustion, r-log-every-send-and-response).

example.title: The three rung texts the artefact describes
example.code:
[polite, T+3, to dana@acme.example, invoice attached] Subject: Invoice 2026-041 (GBP 4,800) — due 15 June
Hi Dana, a quick check on invoice 2026-041 for GBP 4,800, dated 31 May and due 15 June under clause 7.2 of our MSA (net 15); it is 3 days past due today. The PDF is attached in case it did not reach accounts payable. Could you confirm the date it is scheduled for payment? Thanks — Ruslan
[firm, T+10, to dana@acme.example + ap@acme.example, invoice attached] Subject: Invoice 2026-041 (GBP 4,800) — 10 days overdue, payment by 1 July
Dana, Accounts Payable — invoice 2026-041 for GBP 4,800 (issued 31 May, due 15 June, MSA clause 7.2) is now 10 days overdue. Please arrange payment by 1 July. From 16 June the invoice accrues statutory interest under the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998 at 8% over the Bank of England base rate; I would rather not add that to the ledger. PDF attached. — Ruslan
[legal, T+30, email + registered post, to both] Formal notice before action — from Ruslan Faion, 12 Example Road, Lisbon, to Acme Analytics Ltd, 1 Acme Way, London EC1A 1AA. Invoice 2026-041, GBP 4,800.00, due 15 June 2026; statutory interest and compensation under the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998 to date GBP 121.40; total outstanding GBP 4,921.40. Unless payment in full is received within 14 days of the date of this notice I will issue a claim in the County Court without further notice. This letter is sent without prejudice to our working relationship, which I would like to continue.
example.note: The polite text is 84 words with exactly one question; the firm text names one consequence with its statutory basis and no legal threat; the notice carries both addresses, the ledger, the 14-day deadline and the named next step.

example.title: What the validator and the reviewer reject
example.note: Validator output: `$.rungs: 2 items, minItems=3`, `$.rungs[0].offset_days: 1 not in enum [3, 10, 30]`, `$.rungs[0].offset_days: must equal 3, got 1`, `$.rungs[0].word_count: 240 violates maximum=120`, `$.rungs[0].asks_confirmed_payment_date: must equal True, got False`, `$.rungs[0].mentions_fee_or_consequence: must equal False, got True`, `$.rungs[0].mentions_legal_action: must equal False, got True`, `$.rungs[1].pay_by_within_days: 25 violates maximum=7`, `$.rungs[1].recipients: 1 items, minItems=2`, `$.status.halted: must equal True, got False`, `$.status.outstanding_balance: must equal 0, got 4800`.

What the reviewer sees beyond the validator: the "5% weekly late fee" has no clause and `late_payment_basis.kind` is `none`, so the firm rung's consequence is invented (r-fees-and-leverage-only-from-contract-or-statute); the polite rung is scheduled for 2026-06-16, one day after the due date, so it would land before most approval queues have moved (r-three-rungs-clocked-from-due-date).
